info.title: EDUNEXUS API
info.description: Interface release: Section 2B.1 roster import now has a manager screen that previews a CSV, takes explicit duplicate decisions and commits the identical reviewed payload. Earlier interface releases gave screens to the reviewed learner corrections — LRN correction (2B.1), enrollment timeline correction (2B.2), identity links and reversal (2B.3), enrollment void and restoration (2B.4) and grade-placement correction (2B.5) — now have manager screens on the Learner registry and Enrollment screens. Earlier interface releases gave Section 4A.1/4A.2 subjects and offerings and Section 3B.4 manual follow-up their screens. No endpoint, schema, permission or academic behavior changed. Sections 1 through 4B.1: staff/school setup, learner registry/enrollment, roster imports, LRN and timeline corrections, reviewed reversible identity links, and reviewed enrollment void/restoration. Managers maintain the registry; teachers read current assigned learners and may review classroom attendance for accessible learners in their sections. Linked profiles remain manager-readable but frozen; normal lists return retained profiles. Enrollment learner_id identifies the retained profile, while recorded_learner_id preserves original ownership. Identity links never reparent or delete enrollment history; assigned source LRNs and overlapping enrollment years block reconciliation. Effective timelines include corrections, while /history explicitly returns original movements. All review commits require current versions, unchanged context, a reason and explicit confirmation. Closed-year enrollment dates/state remain immutable. Imports use the EDUNEXUS template with stored preview/commit receipts. Enrollment record_state is valid or voided; voided records retain their histories but are excluded from default enrollment lists, teacher access, and annual uniqueness. Timeline/history responses label record_state and usable_for_reporting. Duplicate voids identify a retained same-year enrollment. Restore is blocked by annual conflicts. Grade-placement review corrects a whole-year grade and all timeline sections while preserving dates and movements. Shared correction history labels timeline versus placement revisions and old/new grades; older timeline rows may have null grade metadata. This is not promotion or a midyear grade transition. Reviewed school and section instructional calendars now distinguish classroom, alternative delivery, no-class and suspended AM/PM sessions. Missing dates remain unconfigured. Reads and change batches are limited to 62 dates; school-wide edits block when reviewed section overrides require resolution. Calendar totals count scheduled session categories, not learner attendance or official form credits. Dated attendance sheets and reviewed classroom AM/PM present/absent marks are implemented in batches of up to 100 learners. Null marks remain unknown. Only active years and nonfuture dates accept changes. Managers can read historical rosters; teacher sheets retain current learner-access restrictions and are not complete historical reports. Attendance blocks conflicting calendar, timeline, placement and void corrections until affected marks are reviewed and cleared. Manager monthly readiness review, submission, return, locking and reopening now preserve immutable historical snapshots. Submitted and locked months freeze marks, calendars and roster membership; identity reconciliation involving frozen members is blocked. Teachers see assigned-section workflow status without historical learner snapshots. All overlapping calendar dates must be configured, classroom marks complete, and the clipped month ended before submission; ADM months are blocked. Monthly counts are session counts, not official credits. Read-only classroom absence monitoring now provides 1-31 date windows, current-access teacher scope, filtered cursor pagination, raw session observations, completion gaps and within-window absent-classroom-date runs. Unknowns, ADM and enrollment gaps break runs; explicit nonclass dates skip them. No school alert thresholds, dropout labels or automated messages are assigned. Manual manager-only follow-up now preserves opening evidence, current-evidence comparisons and reviewed action history. One open case is allowed per annual enrollment. Managers can assign active managerial staff, set due dates, update, resolve, cancel and reopen cases; existing cases remain manageable after year closure or source correction. Creation requires matching absence or recording-gap evidence in an active year. Automatic alerts remain disabled because the school has no approved rule. An explicit subject catalog now provides immutable normalized codes, versioned names/kinds/grade applicability, archival and protected change history. No official curriculum, grade weights or numeric Kindergarten policy is seeded. Section offerings pin subject metadata and grade applicability at an explicit catalog version. Managers may add, retire, reactivate and reorder offerings in open years; only draft years permit explicit snapshot refresh. Catalog changes never automatically rewrite section subject details. Teachers read offerings of their current advised open-year sections; no learner permissions are expanded. Manager-only assessment-policy drafts now store explicit Grades 1-6 applicability, source references and 1-10 component weights totaling exactly 10000 integer basis points (100%). Draft and archived states never imply approval, section binding or operational use. Metadata edits preserve immutable history; no formulas, transmutation, rounding, missing-score policy or numeric Kindergarten assessment are supplied. A manager can now record that the school adopted one exact unarchived draft revision for one school year, freezing that revision, an adoption date inside the year and the school record reference that carries the decision. Later draft revisions never change a frozen snapshot, and an adopted draft cannot be archived until its adoption is withdrawn. At most one standing adoption exists per school year and policy; withdrawal is a reviewed one-way action that preserves the frozen revision and journal, after which the policy may be adopted again. An adoption reference is supplied text rather than proof that DepEd or the school approved the content. A manager can now also record which section subject offering a standing adoption governs. Binding requires current offering and adoption versions, one shared school year, an active offering and a section grade the adopted revision applies to. One standing binding exists per offering; release is a reviewed one-way action and rebinding is allowed afterwards. A standing binding blocks withdrawing its adoption and retiring its offering until released, and closed years are read only. Binding is a scoping record. Teachers and managers can now record raw marks against it: a named assessment carries a component code taken from the bound adopted revision, a reporting period of that school year, a sequence unique per offering, period and component, and a maximum score. Raw marks are written in batches of up to 100, each entry against its own version, and an unrecorded learner stays null rather than zero. Clearing a mark keeps its history, lowering a maximum below a recorded mark is refused, and archived tasks and closed years reject entry. Advisers record for their own current sections while managers retain historical access, and both journals are manager-only. A learner who has withdrawn or transferred out is closed to their former adviser for both reading and entry, answering 404, while managers keep the record; an entry must carry the raw_score key explicitly, since only a JSON null clears a mark; and score sheet, entry and history reads append the enrollments they disclosed to the learner access audit. No component total, weighting, percentage, rounding, transmutation, MPS, GWA, subject or section average, or computed grade exists at any endpoint; those wait on the school grading enclosure and ECR examples. ADM participation/conversion, official attendance arithmetic, academic grades, promotion, official forms and closed-year record correction remain unimplemented. Staff invitations are tracked records: a manager requests an email, display name and permission level, then either creates the account or links an identifier the operator provisioned. Creation calls an isolated Edge Function that holds the service-role key and can only invite one address; the API runtime holds no such key and can never alter or delete an identity. A deployment configuring no function answers IDENTITY_SERVICE_DISABLED and keeps the link route, where an unknown identifier is rejected by foreign key. An Auth identity cannot be rolled back with the transaction, so version, state and permission level are all checked before it is created. One open request exists per email, principals may request any permission level while administrative officers may request teachers only, and both completion and cancellation are terminal with immutable history. Password recovery is initiated by the browser against Supabase with the publishable key and answers identically whether or not an address is registered; authenticator reset remains an operator action. Supabase bearer authentication is required; the school did not require a second factor. Calendar dates are YYYY-MM-DD in Asia/Manila; timestamps are UTC. JSON bodies are limited to 32 KiB, except timeline and placement preview/correction POST routes (256 KiB/1000 entries).
